translations.answer: The project maintainer noted that the Boost.Python binding does not automatically complete the required child-to-base identification. It should, like other TSID bindings, explicitly expose constructor overloads for each supported ContactBase subclass. The original author confirmed that the modification works for Contact6d, ContactPoint, and ContactTwoFramePositions; however, this change is only applicable to the user fork commit eb03d05, and no upstream release has been made. The fix is not yet verified in the upstream.
translations.applicability: Applies to the original post TSID Python binding fork; due to unknown version and upstream merge status, the target build must be verified in practice.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The original author initially only exposed the ContactBase& constructor, which failed to instantiate.
translations.details.attempts.1: Subsequently, overloads for Contact6d, ContactPoint, and ContactTwoFramePositions were added via bp::init.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: The binding visitor was found to only expose the ContactBase& constructor, without adding bp::init overloads for specific Contact6d subclass.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: This contrasts with the pattern of other TSID bindings, where each possible child class has an independent method or constructor.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: An explicit constructor overload was added to the TaskContactForceEqualityPythonVisitor for each supported ContactBase subclass, along with corresponding contact header files.
translations.details.environments.0: TSID user fork; Python binding; UR5 force-task example; original post does not provide TSID/Python/Boost versions or OS information.
translations.details.limits.0: The modification is only present in the user fork; no upstream PR has been merged, and no complete working force-control example is available.
translations.details.limits.1: The environment version is not provided, and other TSID/Boost.Python versions must be recompiled and verified.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The original author confirmed that the modification allows instantiation of Contact6d; the fork commit eb03d05 patch aligns with the explanation.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why does the TaskContactForceEquality constructor still report a C++ signature mismatch when Contact6d inherits from ContactBase?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: A successful binding only proves that an object can be constructed, not that force tasks have correct reference, constraint dimension, contact stability, or real-time force limits.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The project maintainer noted that the Python binding did not automatically recognize the inheritance from Contact6d to ContactBase at the constructor location.
translations.details.symptoms.0: TaskContactForceEquality(name, RobotWrapper, dt, Contact6d) raises an ArgumentError, with the C++ signature only showing ContactBase&.
translations.source.locator: TSID #247: Maintainer comment 2568242300 explains subclass overload; author comment 2575770028 confirms instantiation; fork commit eb03d05 includes three constructor overloads
translations.source.title: TSID Python binding needs to explicitly expose constructors for Contact6d and other ContactBase subclasses
